description: Hey everyone! I'm a passionate developer deeply focused on Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and cutting-edge software solutions. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I'm building an innovative, data-driven project leveraging NASA’s open datasets. I'm looking for smart, driven teammates skilled in coding, data analysis, UI/UX design, or space tech who want to build something extraordinary and crush this hackathon together. Let's turn complex space data into real-world impact!
summary: SwarmXplorer is a decentralized multi-agent robotics framework designed for safe, autonomous Martian surface exploration and astronaut Marswalk navigation. Operating without centralized servers or GPS infrastructure, it integrates multi-mission NASA orbital imagery and elevation datasets with 3D volumetric voxel mapping, Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) sensor fusion, and Space-Time Conflict-Based Search (MAPF-CBS). By dynamically allocating mapping tasks across heterogeneous air and ground robot swarms via a Contract Net Protocol, SwarmXplorer generates real-time hazard alerts and collision-free trajectories, empowering astronauts to explore extreme planetary terrains safely and efficiently.
details: - What it does: SwarmXplorer creates a layered, real-time 3D navigation and hazard map for Martian exploration, guiding human astronauts safely during extravehicular activities (Marswalks) in GPS-denied environments. - How it works: Autonomous air and ground agents collaborate via a decentralized P2P mesh network. Using market-based auctions (Contract Net Protocol), agents divide terrain mapping tasks, fuse LiDAR/orbital data through Extended Kalman Filters (EKF), build 3D volumetric voxel grids, and compute collision-free paths using Space-Time A* and MAPF-CBS algorithms. - Tools & Technologies Used: Python, ROS 2, Docker, 3D Volumetric Voxel Mapping, Extended Kalman Filters (EKF), MAPF-CBS Pathfinding, and NASA Open Datasets. - Impact & Creativity: Bridges the gap between robotic reconnaissance and human exploration by providing live terrain updates, blackbox telemetry auditing, and scalable fault-tolerance applicable to Mars, lunar lava tubes, and terrestrial disaster zones.
